confuciusornis:eswiki:17.title: Confuciusornis (Aptitud de vuelo, estilo de vida, comportamiento social, reproducción)

facts.statement: The genus Confuciusornis was formally described by Hou and colleagues in 1995.
facts.quote: authority: Hou et al., 1995

facts.statement: Confuciusornis lived in China between 125 and 120 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis is a genus of basal crow-sized avialan confuciusornithid theropod dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous Period of the Yixian and Jiufotang Formations of China, dating from 125 to 120 million years ago.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis possessed a toothless beak similar to that of modern birds.
facts.quote: Like modern birds, Confuciusornis had a toothless beak

facts.statement: Several hundred complete specimens of Confuciusornis have been found, making it one of the most abundant vertebrates in the Yixian Formation.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis is one of the most abundant vertebrates found in the Yixian Formation, and several hundred complete specimens have been found.

facts.statement: The discovery of Confuciusornis began in November 1993 when paleontologists Hou Lianhai and Hu Yoaming were shown a fossil bird specimen by collector Zhang He.
facts.quote: In November 1993, the Chinese paleontologists Hou Lianhai and Hu Yoaming of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology (IVPP) at Beijing, visited fossil collector Zhang He at his home in Jinzhou, where he showed them a fossil bird specimen that he had bought at a local flea market.

facts.statement: The species Confuciusornis sanctus was formally described in 1995 based on three specimens.
facts.quote: In 1995, these two specimens, as well as a third one, were formally described as a new genus and species of bird, Confuciusornis sanctus, by Hou and colleagues.

facts.statement: The name Confuciusornis combines the Chinese philosopher Confucius with the Greek word for bird.
facts.quote: The generic name combines the philosopher Confucius with Greek ὄρνις (ornis), "bird".

facts.statement: The specific name sanctus means "holy one" in Latin, referencing Confucius as a sage.
facts.quote: The specific name means "holy one" in Latin and is a translation of Chinese 圣贤 (shèngxián), "sage", again in reference to Confucius.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, catalogued as IVPP V10918, consists of a partial skeleton including a skull and parts of the forelimb.
facts.quote: The first discovered specimen was designated the holotype and catalogued under the specimen number IVPP V10918; it comprises a partial skeleton with skull and parts of the forelimb.

facts.statement: By 2010, the Shandong Tianyu Museum of Nature held 536 specimens of Confuciusornis.
facts.quote: In 1999, it was estimated that the National Geological Museum of China in Beijing housed nearly 100 specimens of Confuciusornis, and in 2010, the Shandong Tianyu Museum of Nature was reported to possess 536 specimens of the bird.

facts.statement: Forty individuals of Confuciusornis were found on a 100 m² surface, suggesting entire flocks were killed by volcanic ash, heat, or gas.
facts.quote: At one time forty individuals were discovered on a surface of about 100 m2. This has been explained as the result of entire flocks of birds being simultaneously killed by ash, heat or poisonous gas following the volcanic eruptions that caused the tuff stone in which the fossils were found to be deposited as lake sediments.

facts.statement: It is debated whether two paratype specimens belong to Confuciusornis sanctus because their bones do not overlap with the holotype.
facts.quote: It was soon noted that the two paratype specimens only comprise bones that are unknown from the holotype, and that this lack of overlap makes their referral to the species speculative.

facts.statement: The species Confuciusornis chuonzhous was named by Hou in 1997 using specimen IVPP V10919, which was originally a paratype of C. sanctus.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis chuonzhous was named by Hou in 1997 based on specimen IVPP V10919, originally a paratype of C. sanctus.

facts.statement: The species Confuciusornis suniae was named by Hou in 1997 based on specimen IVPP V11308.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis suniae, named by Hou in the same 1997 publication, was based on specimen IVPP V11308.

facts.statement: The species Confuciusornis dui was named by Hou and colleagues in 1999.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis dui was named by Hou and colleagues in 1999.

facts.statement: The holotype of Confuciusornis dui (IVPP V11553) is a nearly complete adult skeleton featuring long tail feathers and an impression of a horny beak.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen (IVPP V11553) is a nearly complete skeleton of an adult that includes a pair of long tail feathers and the impression of the horny beak.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis dui was described as smaller and more gracile than other specimens, with its holotype being approximately 15% smaller than the C. sanctus holotype and 30% smaller than large C. sanctus individuals.
facts.quote: C. dui was smaller and more gracile than most other Confuciusornis specimens, with the holotype being ca. 15% smaller than the holotype of C. sanctus and ca. 30% smaller than larger individuals of that species.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis feducciai was distinguished from other species by its larger size, different skeletal proportions, and various morphological features.
facts.quote: C. feducciai differed from other Confuciusornis species in its larger size, skeletal proportions, and a number of morphological features.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis was roughly the size of a modern crow, measuring about 50 cm in total length with a wingspan of up to 70 cm.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis was about the size of a modern crow, with a total length of 50 cm and a wingspan of up to 70 cm.

facts.statement: The body weight of Confuciusornis has been estimated to range from 0.2 kg to 0.5 kg.
facts.quote: Its body weight has been estimated to have been as much as 0.5 kg, or as little as 0.2 kg.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis feducciai was approximately one-third longer than average specimens of C. sanctus.
facts.quote: C. feducciai was about a third longer than average specimens of C. sanctus.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis possessed advanced traits like a short tail with a pygostyle and a bony sternum, but retained primitive features such as large forelimb claws, a skull with a closed eye-socket, and a small breastbone.
facts.quote: It was more "advanced" or derived than Archaeopteryx in possessing a short tail with a pygostyle (a bone formed from a series of short, fused tail vertebrae) and a bony sternum (breastbone), but more basal or "primitive" than modern birds in retaining large claws on the forelimbs, having a primitive skull with a closed eye-socket, and a relatively small breastbone.

facts.statement: Unlike most species found in the Yixian Formation, Confuciusornis jianchangensis was discovered in the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: In contrast to most other species, which stem from the Yixian Formation, C. jianchangensis is found in the Jiufotang Formation.

facts.statement: A 2011 statistical analysis suggested that differences in C. dui might be individual variations within C. sanctus rather than distinct species, though the validity remains debated due to the potential loss of the holotype.
facts.quote: A statistical analysis by Marguán-Lobon and colleagues in 2011 revealed no significant differences to specimens referred to the smallest size class of C. sanctus, suggesting that the supposed differences are individual variations of a single species.

facts.statement: Marguán-Lobon and colleagues (2011) argued that C. feducciai is identical to C. sanctus, citing the presence of a humeral opening in the holotype and statistical overlap within the variation of C. sanctus.
facts.quote: Marguán-Lobon and colleagues, in 2011, argued that this diagnosis is problematic. The large opening in the humerus, although apparently absent in the left humerus, was clearly present in the right humerus of the holotype. Furthermore, their statistical analysis found the specimen to fall well within the continuum of variation of C. sanctus. These authors therefore proposed that C. feducciai is identical (a junior synonym) of C. sanctus.

facts.statement: The skull of Confuciusornis was near triangular in side view with a robust, toothless, and pointed beak.
facts.quote: The skull was near triangular in side view, and the toothless beak was robust and pointed.

facts.statement: A straight tomial crest ran along the entire length of the upper jaw, serving as a bony support for the cutting edge.
facts.quote: The tomial crest of the upper jaw (a bony support for the jaw's cutting edge) was straight for its entire length.

facts.statement: The eye socket was large and round, containing scleral plates that provided bony support inside the eye.
facts.quote: The orbit was large, round, and contained scleral plates (the bony support inside the eye).

facts.statement: A prominent flange formed the upper border of the eye socket and continued as a postorbital process with outward-projecting crests that expanded the rim of the orbit.
facts.quote: A prominent supraorbital flange formed the upper border of the orbit, and continued as the postorbital process, which had prominent crests which projected outwards to the sides, forming an expansion of the orbit's rim.

facts.statement: The lower jaw is one of the best-preserved skull parts and was particularly robust at the front third of its length.
facts.quote: The mandible (lower jaw) is one of the best preserved parts of the skull. It was robust, especially at the front third of its length.

facts.statement: The splenial bone was three-pronged, similar to some modern birds but unlike the simple version found in Archaeopteryx, with its lower margin following the jaw's edge.
facts.quote: The splenial bone was three-pronged (as in some modern birds, but unlike the simple splenial of Archaeopteryx), and its lower margin followed the lower margin of the mandible.

facts.statement: The holotype of C. dui had an upwards-curving beak that sharply tapered to the tip, whereas a C. sanctus specimen had an almost straight upper margin and a tip slightly hooked downwards.
facts.quote: The holotype of C. dui preserves the outline of an upwards curving beak which sharply tapers towards its tip, while a C. sanctus specimen (IVPP V12352) has an upper margin that is almost straight, and a tip that appears to be slightly hooked downwards.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis specimens show a variable number of neck vertebrae, with some having eight and others nine.
facts.quote: The various specimens seem to have a variable number of neck vertebrae, some showing eight, others nine.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis had at least twelve back vertebrae.
facts.quote: There were at least twelve back vertebrae.

facts.statement: While earlier descriptions counted four or five free tail vertebrae, a 1999 study by Chiappe and colleagues reported seven.
facts.quote: Although earlier descriptions had counted four or five "free", not fused, tail vertebrae, Chiappe e.a. in 1999 reported seven of them.

facts.statement: The tail of Confuciusornis ended in a pygostyle, which is a complete fusion of the last vertebrae.
facts.quote: The tail ended in a pygostyle, a complete fusion of the last vertebrae.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis possessed an exceptionally large humerus, or upper arm bone.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis had an exceptionally large humerus (upper arm bone).

facts.statement: The sternum of Confuciusornis was relatively broad with a low keel that was raised at the back end.
facts.quote: The sternum was relatively broad and had a low keel which was raised at the back end.

facts.statement: The sideways orientation of the shoulder joint in Confuciusornis meant it could not lift its wings high above its back.
facts.quote: The orientation of the shoulder joint was sideways, instead of angled upward as in modern birds; this means that Confuciusornis was unable to lift its wings high above its back.

facts.statement: A 2006 study by Phil Senter suggested the shoulder joint was pointed largely downwards, preventing the humerus from being lifted above the horizontal.
facts.quote: According to a study by Phil Senter in 2006, the joint was even pointed largely downwards meaning that the humerus could not be lifted above the horizontal.

facts.statement: The second metacarpal supporting flight feathers in Confuciusornis was very heavily built and carried a small claw.
facts.quote: The second metacarpal, which supported the flight feathers, was very heavily built; its finger carries a small claw.

facts.statement: The claw of the first finger in Confuciusornis was very large and curved.
facts.quote: The claw of the first finger to the contrary was very large and curved.

facts.statement: The phalangeal formula for the fingers of Confuciusornis was 2-3-4-0-0.
facts.quote: The formula of the finger phalanges was 2-3-4-0-0.

facts.statement: The first metatarsal in Confuciusornis supported a first toe or hallux that pointed backward.
facts.quote: The first metatarsal was attached to the lower shaft of the second and supported a first toe or hallux, pointing to the back.

facts.statement: The phalangeal formula for the toes of Confuciusornis was 2-3-4-5-0.
facts.quote: The formula of the toe phalanges was 2-3-4-5-0.

facts.statement: The toe proportions suggest Confuciusornis used them for walking and perching, while the large claws on the thumb and third finger were likely used for climbing.
facts.quote: The proportions of the toes suggest that they were used for both walking and perching, while the large claws of the thumb and third finger were probably used for climbing.

facts.statement: The wing feathers of Confuciusornis were long and appeared modern.
facts.quote: The wing feathers of Confuciusornis were long and modern in appearance.

facts.statement: In a 0.5-kilogram individual, the primary wing feathers of Confuciusornis reached 20.7 centimetres in length.
facts.quote: The primary wing feathers of a 0.5-kilogram individual reached 20.7 centimetres in length.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis lacked an alula, or "bastard wing", unlike some more advanced birds.
facts.quote: Unlike some more advanced birds, Confuciusornis lacked an alula, or "bastard wing".

facts.statement: The forearm bones of Confuciusornis lacked any indication of quill knobs or bony attachment points for feather ligaments.
facts.quote: The forearm bones lacked any indication of quill knobs (papillae ulnares), or bony attachment points for the feather ligaments.

facts.statement: Many individuals of Confuciusornis lacked the two long tail feathers, possibly due to sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: Many individuals of Confuciusornis lacked even these two tail feathers, possibly due to sexual dimorphism.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis was the first early bird fossil to show preserved pheomelanosomes, though a second team failed to find these traces.
facts.quote: It was also the first time an early bird fossil has been shown to contain preserved pheomelanosomes.

facts.statement: Male Confuciusornis likely had long tail feathers that were dark in color along their entire length.
facts.quote: The long tail feathers of male specimens would have also been dark in color along their entire length.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis possessed large fleshy foot pads and curved claws similar to modern tree-dwelling birds, suggesting it may have had a similar lifestyle.
facts.quote: The large, fleshy phalangeal foot pads, small interphalangeal foot pads, presence of only reticulate scales on the underside of the foot (which increases flexibility), and curved foot claws of Confuciusornis are all traits shared with modern tree-dwelling, perching birds, suggesting that Confuciusornis may have had a similar lifestyle.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis had adaptations for flight including a fused wrist, short tail, ossified sternum with a keel, strut-like coracoid, large deltopectoral crest, strong ulna, and enlarged second metacarpal.
facts.quote: Other adaptations for improved flight capabilities include: a fused wrist, a short tail, an ossified sternum with a central keel, a strut-like coracoid, a large deltopectoral crest, a strong ulna (forearm bone) and an enlarged second metacarpal.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis may have had a different flight stroke and was likely not capable of flight for extended periods due to its inability to rotate its arm behind the body and smaller sternal keel.
facts.quote: However, it may have had a different flight stroke due to being incapable of rotating its arm behind the body, and its relatively smaller sternal keel indicates that it likely was not capable of flight for extended periods of time.

facts.statement: In 2010, Nudds and Dyke argued that the rachis of Confuciusornis feathers were too weak for true flapping flight, suggesting only gliding or parachuting.
facts.quote: In 2010, Robert Nudds and Gareth Dyke published a study arguing that in both Confuciusornis and Archaeopteryx, the raches (central shafts) of the primary feathers were too thin and weak to have remained rigid during the power stroke required for true flight.

facts.statement: In 2016, Falk et al. used laser fluorescence evidence to argue that Confuciusornis was capable of powered flight, contradicting earlier claims of weak feathers.
facts.quote: In 2016, Falk et al. argued in favor of flight capabilities for Confuciusornis using evidence from laser fluorescence of two soft tissue-preserving specimens.

facts.statement: Hou assigned Confuciusornis to the family Confuciusornithidae in 1995.
facts.quote: Hou assigned Confuciusornis to the Confuciusornithidae in 1995.

facts.statement: Hou later concluded that Confuciusornis was the sister taxon of Enantiornithes within the larger group Sauriurae, though this was heavily criticized.
facts.quote: Later he understood that Confuciusornis was not an enantiornithean but concluded it was the sister taxon of the Enantiornithes, within a larger Sauriurae.

facts.statement: In 2001, Ji Qiang suggested Confuciusornis was the sister taxon of Ornithothoraces.
facts.quote: In 2001, Ji Qiang suggested an alternative position as the sister taxon of the Ornithothoraces.

facts.statement: In 2002, Chiappe confirmed Ji's hypothesis by defining the group Pygostylia, with Confuciusornis as its most basal member.
facts.quote: In 2002 Ji's hypothesis was confirmed by a cladistic analysis by Chiappe, who defined a new group: the Pygostylia of which Confuciusornis is by definition the most basal member.

facts.statement: A controversial study suggested Confuciusornis was more closely related to Microraptor and dromaeosaurids than Archaeopteryx, but this was criticized on methodological grounds.
facts.quote: One controversial study concluded that Confuciusornis may be more closely related to Microraptor and other dromaeosaurids than to Archaeopteryx, but this study was criticized on methodological grounds.

facts.statement: Researchers questioned rachis measurements, noting shaft thicknesses of 2.1-2.3 mm in their specimens compared to the 1.2 mm reported by Nudds and Dyke.
facts.quote: A number of researchers have questioned the correctness of the rachis measurements, stating that the specimens they had studied showed a shaft thickness of 2.1 - 2.3 mm, compared to 1.2 mm as reported by Nudds and Dyke.

facts.statement: Nudds and Dyke assumed Confuciusornis weighed 500 g, similar to a modern teal.
facts.quote: Nudds and Dyke assumed a weight of 500 g for Confuciusornis, as heavy as the modern teal.

facts.statement: Paul argued a more reasonable weight estimate for Confuciusornis is about 180 g, less than a pigeon.
facts.quote: Paul argued that a more reasonable body weight estimate is about 180 g, less than that of a pigeon.

facts.statement: In 1998, Larry Martin and colleagues reported that long tail feathers were found in about 5 to 10% of known specimens.
facts.quote: Larry Martin and colleagues stated in 1998 that long tail feathers are present in about 5 to 10% of the specimens known at the time.

facts.statement: Peters and Petters suggested that Confuciusornis may have shed tail feathers as a defense mechanism triggered by stress from volcanic explosions.
facts.quote: Peters and Petters, on the other hand, suggested that Confuciusornis may have shed the feathers as a defense mechanism, a method used by several extant species.

facts.statement: In 2011, Jesús Marugán-Lobón and colleagues proposed that the variation in tail feathers might indicate the existence of two separate species.
facts.quote: In a 2011 paper, Jesús Marugán-Lobón and colleagues stated that even the presence of two separate species, one with and one without long tail feathers, needs to be considered.

facts.statement: In 2016, Luis Chiappe and Meng Qingjin estimated a maximum egg diameter of 23 mm based on the pelvic aperture of a large specimen.
facts.quote: In a 2016 book, Luis Chiappe and Meng Qingjin stated that the aperture of a large specimen (DNHM-D 2454) indicates a maximum egg diameter of 23 mm.

facts.statement: In 2007, Gary Kaiser argued that Confuciusornis likely nested in tree crevices rather than open nests and that the small egg size suggests large clutch sizes.
facts.quote: Kaiser, in 2007, argued that Confuciusornis likely did not brood in an open nest but might have used crevices in trees for protection, and that the small size of the only known egg indicates large clutch sizes.

facts.statement: In 2016, David Varricchio and Frankie Jackson argued that Mesozoic birds like Confuciusornis likely buried their eggs on the ground rather than nesting above ground.
facts.quote: In contrast, a 2016 review by David Varricchio and Frankie Jackson argued that nesting above the ground evolved only at a much later stage, within Neornithes, and that Mesozoic birds would have buried their eggs on the ground, either fully or partially, as seen in non-avian dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Subsequent studies contested the link between slow bone growth and low metabolic rates in Mesozoic birds, suggesting it resulted from decreasing body size instead.
facts.quote: This view was contested by subsequent studies, which pointed out that slow growing bone is not necessarily an indicator for low metabolic rates, and in the case of Mesozoic birds was rather a result of the decrease in body size that characterized the early evolution of birds.

facts.statement: Peters and Peters concluded the size classes represented sexes rather than growth stages because two distinct growth spurts are unseen in known amniotes.
facts.quote: As it would be highly unlikely that Confuciusornis showed two distinct growth spurts, a feature unseen in known amniotes, they concluded that the two larger size classes represented the two sexes rather than growth stages (sexual size dimorphism).

facts.statement: Chiappe and colleagues suggested growth periods likely took several years, similar to the modern kiwi, contradicting the short growth phase proposed by de Ricqlès.
facts.quote: Thus, growth periods must have been longer than in modern birds and likely took several years, as is true for the modern kiwi.

facts.statement: Chiappe and colleagues concluded in 2008 that limb bone growth was almost isometric, meaning skeletal proportions did not change during growth.
facts.quote: Chiappe and colleagues, in their 2008 study, concluded that limb bones growth was almost isometric, meaning that skeletal proportions did not change during growth.

facts.statement: Peters and Peters observed in 2009 that wing bones were proportionally longer in small individuals, suggesting allometric growth similar to modern chickens.
facts.quote: Peters and Peters in 2009, who observed that wing bones tended to be proportionally longer in very small individuals, as seen in modern chicken, and thus grew allometrically.

facts.statement: Chiappe and colleagues responded in 2010 that proportional variation existed across all sizes and that allometry was not conclusively demonstrated by Peters and Peters' analyses.
facts.quote: Chiappe and colleagues, in their 2010 comment, responded that proportional variation is present across the whole size range, and that the presence of allometry was not conclusively demonstrated by the analyses presented by Peters and Peters.

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that the presence of medullary bone in a Confuciusornis specimen indicated it was a female, as this tissue serves as a calcium reservoir for egg production in modern birds.
facts.quote: In modern birds, medullary bone only forms temporarily in females, where it functions as a calcium reservoir for eggshell production.

facts.statement: A studied female Confuciusornis specimen showed evidence of at least three years of growth, indicating an extended development period similar to non-avian dinosaurs.
facts.quote: At least two lines of arrested growth (growth lines that form annually) could be identified, demonstrating an extended growth over several years; the studied female would have been in its third year.

facts.statement: Small Confuciusornis individuals possessed long tail feathers, suggesting that sexual maturity was reached well before the animals achieved their maximum size.
facts.quote: Long tail feathers were confirmed to occur in small individuals, the smallest of which was only around 23% the mass of the largest specimens.

facts.statement: A 2018 study questioned the identification of medullary bone in Confuciusornis, noting that the tissue was found in the forelimb whereas it is typically located in the hind limb of modern birds.
facts.quote: In a 2018 study, Jingmai O'Connor and colleagues questioned the identification of medullary bone, arguing that the purported medullary bone was only found in the forelimb, while in modern birds it is mostly present in the hind limb.

facts.statement: In 1999, researchers suggested Confuciusornis was likely herbivorous based on its upward-curving, non-raptorial beak, although no stomach contents were known at the time.
facts.quote: In 1999, Chinese paleontologist Lianhai Hou and colleagues suggested that Confuciusornis was likely herbivorous, though no stomach contents were yet known, pointing out that the beak curved upwards and was not raptorial.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Dieter S. Peters compared Confuciusornis to the white-tailed tropicbird, noting similarities in long tails, narrow wings, and nesting habits near volcanoes.
facts.quote: Peters thought that it could be best compared with the white-tailed tropicbird (Phaeton lepturus), a fisher that too has a long tail and narrow wings—and even often nests in the neighbourhood of volcanoes.

facts.statement: In 2002, Andrzej Elżanowski proposed that Confuciusornis foraged on the wing from water or ground surfaces rather than in tree crowns, citing its long wings and leg proportions.
facts.quote: Andrzej Elżanowski, in 2002, found it unlikely that a long-winged and short-legged bird like Confuciusornis would forage in tree crowns, and instead proposed that it foraged on the wing, seizing prey from the water or ground surface.

facts.statement: A 2006 study described a Confuciusornis specimen preserving the vertebrae and ribs of a small fish, suggesting the bird may have included fish in its diet.
facts.quote: In 2006, Johan Dalsätt and colleagues described a C. sanctus specimen (IVPP V13313) from the Jiufotang Beds which preserves seven to nine vertebrae and several ribs of a small fish, probably Jinanichthys.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that the discovery of fish bones did not support a herbivorous diet for Confuciusornis, especially since no specimens have been found with gastroliths used for digesting plant fibers.
facts.quote: Though it is unknown how common fish were in the diet of Confuciusornis, the finding did not support a herbivorous diet, and the researchers pointed out that no specimens have been found with gastroliths (stomach stones), which are swallowed by birds to help digest plant fibers.

facts.statement: Based on the lack of gastroliths and the presence of fish remains, researchers suggested Confuciusornis was likely omnivorous, similar to crows.
facts.quote: Instead, they suggested it would have been omnivorous, similar to for example crows.

facts.statement: The skull of Confuciusornis was relatively immobile and lacked the kinesis found in modern birds, which allows them to raise their snouts relative to the back of the skull.
facts.quote: The skull was relatively immobile, incapable of the kinesis of modern birds that can raise the snout relative to the back of the skull.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis fossils were discovered in the Yixian and Jiufotang Formations and are part of the Jehol Biota.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis was discovered in the Yixian and Jiufotang Formations and is a member of the Jehol Biota.

facts.statement: A 2010 study using oxygen isotopes estimated the mean air temperature of the Yixian Formation, where Confuciusornis lived, to be 10 °C ± 4 °C, indicating a cool temperate climate.
facts.quote: Using oxygen isotopes in reptile bones found in the formation, a 2010 study determined that many formations from East Asia, including the Yixian, had a cool temperate climate. The mean air temperature of the Yixian Formation was estimated at 10 °C ± 4 °C.

facts.statement: The genus Confuciusornis was established by Hou and colleagues in 1995.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Hou et al., 1995

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Confuciusornis is Confuciusornis sanctus.
facts.quote: type_species: Confuciusornis sanctus

facts.statement: Jinzhouornis has been proposed as a synonym for Confuciusornis by Hou and colleagues in 2002.
facts.quote: synonyms: ¿Jinzhouornis? Hou et al., 2002

facts.statement: Confuciusornis lived in what is now China during the Late Early Cretaceous, approximately 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis es un género de aves prehistóricas del tamaño de un cuervo, que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico Inferior (hace aproximadamente 120 millones de años) en lo que hoy es China.

facts.statement: Like modern birds, Confuciusornis had a toothless beak, suggesting that tooth loss evolved convergently in this genus and other contemporary birds.
facts.quote: Al igual que las aves modernas, Confuciusornis tenía un pico sin dientes, aunque algunos parientes cercanos de las aves modernas tales como Hesperornis e Ichthyornis sí tenían dientes, lo que indicaría que la pérdida de ellos ocurrió convergentemente en Confuciusornis y en las aves contemporáneas.

facts.statement: The recognized species of Confuciusornis include C. sanctus, C. dui, C. chuonzhous, and C. suniae, with the latter two possibly being synonyms of C. sanctus.
facts.quote: Las especies reconocidas son C. sanctus (especie tipo del género), C. dui, C. chuonzhous y C. suniae (las dos últimas probablemente pueden considerarse sinónimos de C. sanctus).

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analyses suggest Confuciusornis is more closely related to Microraptor and other dromaeosaurids than to Archaeopteryx, and it definitely did not evolve from Archaeopteryx.
facts.quote: Análisis cladísticos recientes indican que Confuciusornis está más relacionado con Microraptor y otros dromeosáuridos que con Archaeopteryx; en cualquier caso, es seguro que no evolucionó a partir de Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis was the size of a modern crow or pigeon, with a wingspan of up to 70 cm and an estimated weight of up to 1.5 kg or less than 0.2 kg depending on the author.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis tenía el tamaño de un cuervo o una paloma modernos, con una envergadura de hasta 70 cm y un peso estimado de hasta 1,5 kg o menos de 0,2 kg, según diferentes autores.

facts.statement: The skull of Confuciusornis shows an unusual combination of features, including a toothless beak like modern birds, while other more modern birds like Liaoningornis and Yanornis still had teeth.
facts.quote: El cráneo presenta una inusual combinación de características: mientras que el pico de Confuciusornis al igual que el pico de las aves actuales no poseía dientes, otras aves más modernas como Liaoningornis y Yanornis en cambio todavía tenían dientes.

facts.statement: The back of the Confuciusornis head was shaped like diapsid reptiles, with two pairs of cranial openings (infratemporal and supratemporal) located behind the eye sockets.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, la zona posterior de la cabeza estaba conformada en forma similar que en los reptiles diápsidos: dos pares de aberturas craneanas (infratemporal y supratemporal) se ubicaban por detrás de las aberturas oculares (órbitas).

facts.statement: The flight apparatus of Confuciusornis was more developed than that of Archaeopteryx, with some specimens showing a keel on the sternum similar to that of modern birds.
facts.quote: El aparato de vuelo de Confuciusornis era más desarrollado que el de Archaeopteryx: el esternón de algunos de los ejemplares presenta un empeine que tiene alguna semejanza a la quilla que poseen las aves modernas.

facts.statement: Confuciusornis is the oldest flying dinosaur with an almost modern flight apparatus.
facts.quote: Confuciusornis es el dinosaurio volador más antiguo con un aparato de vuelo casi moderno.

facts.statement: Between 5% and 10% of Confuciusornis specimens show fossil impressions indicating a pair of long tail feathers.
facts.quote: Entre el 5 al 10 % de los ejemplares de Confuciusornis muestran impresiones fósiles indicativas de un par de largas plumas de cola.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the long tail feathers represent a difference between genders; if correct, this would be the oldest evidence of sexual dimorphism in birds.
facts.quote: Varios estudiosos consideran esta una diferencia entre géneros. Si dicha teoría fuera correcta, sería este el indicio más antiguo de dimorfismo sexual en aves.

facts.statement: Female mate choice in Confuciusornis may have been efficient if males participated in chick care, such as protecting the offspring.
facts.quote: La elección de su compañero por parte de la hembra era apropiado y eficiente si el macho tomaba parte del cuidado de los pichones, por ejemplo, si el macho se encargaba de proteger las crías de la hembra que fecunda.

facts.statement: Researcher De Ricqlès determined that the growth period of Confuciusornis was approximately 20 weeks or slightly less.
facts.quote: Mediante el uso de técnicas de histología ósea, De Ricqlès demostró que el período de crecimiento del "Confuciusornis" era de unas 20 semanas o un poco menos.

facts.statement: Analysis of fibrous lamellae in Confuciusornis indicates that early birds possessed rapid growth phases and high metabolic rates, contrary to previous acceptance.
facts.quote: Aun así el análisis de las laminillas fibrosas del Confuciusornis muestra que en contra de lo aceptado previamente, las aves plesiomórficas ya presentaban (al igual que sus antecesores y descendientes) fases de crecimiento rápido, contando con un metabolismo lo suficientemente elevado para sostener altos ritmos de crecimiento.

facts.statement: One theory suggests that Confuciusornis and similar early birds had extremely precocial traits, capable of flying shortly after hatching, based on comparisons with Gobipteryx embryos.
facts.quote: Según esta teoría, dado que los embriones fósiles del ave del cretácico Gobipteryx presentan un esqueleto del ala con un alto nivel de osificación es que se piensa, que los representantes de este tipo y probablemente las aves plesiomórficas habrían tenido características precociales extremadamente prematuras, teniendo la capacidad de comenzar a volar muy poco tiempo después de romper el cascarón.

facts.statement: Members of the family Confuciusornithidae belong to the Pygostylia group of basal birds.
facts.quote: Los miembros de la familia Confuciusornithidae pertenecen al grupo Pygostylia de formas originales.

facts.statement: All representatives of modern bird orders are descendants of the Pygostylia group.
facts.quote: Todos los representantes de los órdenes de aves modernas son descendientes de este grupo.
